name: Wine Glass
tldr: 🍷 suggests a slow drink across a table, often turning a simple invitation into a date.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🍷 can simply refer to wine as part of a meal or plans to drink wine.
🍷 is shorthand for a relaxed drink with enough time to sit down and talk.
contextMeanings.example: long dinner and a slow wine tonight 🍷

contextMeanings.meaning: 🍷 often proposes an intimate, sit-down drink that feels more like a date than a quick stop.
contextMeanings.example: want to grab some wine thursday? 🍷

contextMeanings.meaning: 🍷 in a coworker chat can suggest moving the conversation away from work and into drinks.
contextMeanings.example: happy to take this offline for a drink 🍷

platformNotes.note: In a direct iMessage thread, a lone 🍷 often functions as an invitation rather than decoration. In a friend chat, it can still sound more intimate than 🍻, so the relationship matters as much as the wording.
On Instagram, 🍷 in direct messages can stand in for a proposed dinner or drinks. In comments, the surrounding post usually supplies the context, so the glass alone carries less of the invitation.
On TikTok, younger viewers tend to read 🍷 as a romantic plan, consistent with its use as the date drink. A standalone glass in a comment can therefore sound like an invitation rather than a reaction.
In Slack, 🍷 in a coworker channel can make the sender sound as if they are steering the chat into drinks after work. Put the invitation in a direct message or use 🍻 for a looser group hang.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z reads 🍷 readily as a date with romantic weight. It is the default choice when a drink should feel intimate rather than casual.
Millennials parse 🍷 easily, but often expect a sentence beside it when the meal or evening matters. In a dating thread, it still suggests a slow evening across a table.

For Gen X readers, the surrounding relationship still matters: 🍷 can be understood as a drink choice in a dating thread, but it may not suggest the same romantic invitation to everyone. Spelling out the plan is safer than assuming it.

warnings.title: Too intimate for a friend hang
warnings.description: 🍷 in a friend thread can make an ordinary catch-up sound overly serious or intimate. Use 🍻 when the intention is simply to get together and have a few drinks.

warnings.title: Coworkers may hear an escape from work
warnings.description: A wine suggestion in a coworker chat can read as the sender trying to leave work behind rather than continue talking about work. Clarify that it is a team celebration or make the invitation outside the work thread.

seoDescription: What does 🍷 mean? It suggests a slow drink across a table, often making an invitation feel like a date rather than a casual hangout.

longForm.overview:
The 🍷 emoji suggests a slow drink rather than a quick stop. Its familiar image of one person with a glass points toward sitting across from someone and talking for a while. That makes it especially useful after “what are we doing?”: “wine?” already imagines a proper evening at a restaurant, wine bar, or similar place. The emoji compresses that invitation into one character and removes the awkwardness of asking someone to spend an evening together.

It is not neutral, though. In dating threads, 🍷 sets the pace more strongly than 🍻 does and usually implies a place where you can sit. 🍸 suggests a newer night out at a trendy cocktail place, while 🍻 fits a friend hang more naturally. Stacking 🍷 with 🍫 turns the invite into a deliberately intimate evening, while 🍷 and 🧀 makes it feel deliberately sophisticated. The key question is not whether the person likes wine, but whether the relationship can carry the extra intimacy implied by the glass.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🍷 usually appears when someone proposes a drink with time to sit and talk, not a quick stop. In a dating thread, “wine thursday? 🍷” lets the emoji carry the invitation. Pairing it with 🍫 adds dessert and makes the evening sound more intentional; 🍷🧀 makes it feel like a wine bar or elevated dinner.

In a friend thread, the same emoji can make the sender sound slightly more intimate than the hang they had in mind, which is why 🍻 is safer for friends. In a coworker thread, it can sound like leaving work behind. “🍷?” leaves room for the recipient to accept or decline.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
🍷 misfires when the relationship is less intimate than the message sounds. Sending it in a friend thread can read as taking an ordinary catch-up too seriously, especially if the recipient was expecting something cheap and casual. In a coworker chat, it can look like the sender is pivoting away from work rather than continuing the work conversation.

It is also risky when the sender means only “I had a glass of wine.” Without other context, the emoji can introduce a date invitation that was never intended. Use 🍻 for a loose drink with friends, and for literal wine references add a plain sentence: “we split a bottle with dinner 🍷.” That tells the recipient which meaning you meant.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🍷, treat it as a proposal first: “yes, thursday works” answers the invitation directly. A question mark beside the glass usually leaves room for a yes, so saying no plainly is fine, but “too formal for us?” can clear up the social temperature without making the exchange awkward.

If the suggestion came from you, adding 🍫 or 🧀 makes it more deliberately intimate or sophisticated. If 🍷 lands on your own message and seems too polished, soften it with 🍻 or add “just grabbing a drink.” In a dating thread, concrete time and place help more than stacking more drink emojis.

faqs.question: What does 🍷 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Usually, he is proposing a slow drink and creating a plan that feels like a date. It signals interest, but it does not prove romantic intent if you do not already know the relationship.

faqs.question: Is 🍷 flirty?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. 🍷 suggests an intimate evening across a table, while 🍻 is more commonly used for a casual drink with friends.

faqs.question: What does 🍷 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: For Gen Z viewers, 🍷 usually suggests a romantic plan or a drink with someone they are interested in. A standalone glass can feel like an invitation rather than a simple reaction.

faqs.question: What does 🍷 mean compared with 🍸?
faqs.answer: 🍷 suggests a slower, more established drink at a place where you can sit together. 🍸 points more toward a trendy cocktail venue, a quicker night out, or a newer relationship.

conversationExamples.message: are we still on for thursday? maybe wine and dessert 🍷🍫
conversationExamples.interpretation: This asks for an intimate evening rather than a quick drink. Respond with a time and place, or suggest a different plan if dessert does not appeal.

conversationExamples.message: wanna grab wine and talk for a couple hours? 🍷
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender wants a relaxed catch-up, though 🍷 can make it sound slightly more intimate than an ordinary friend hang. If that was not the intention, 🍻 would be more natural.

conversationExamples.message: the launch is finally done. drinks after? 🍷
conversationExamples.interpretation: This may be a genuine work celebration, but the wine can also sound like the sender is leaving the work conversation behind. Clarifying that the whole team is coming makes it feel less like a personal pivot.

conversationExamples.message: are we still doing the wine bar for dinner? 🍷
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the glass identifies the planned venue and the wine being served. A direct answer about the reservation is more useful than interpreting it as romantic language.

conversationExamples.message: hosting a wine and cheese thing at 7, bring a bottle 🍷🧀
conversationExamples.interpretation: The pairing makes the invitation feel polished and elevated, especially for an established friendship or small group. Confirming the time and what guests should bring keeps the plan clear.
